name: Green and blue ammonia
principle: Hydrogen and nitrogen are compressed and reacted over an iron catalyst in a Haber-Bosch synthesis loop. Green ammonia takes hydrogen from electrolysis on renewable power and nitrogen from an air separation unit; blue ammonia uses reforming with CO2 capture, where the CO2 is already separated in the process.

advantages: Established product with global shipping and storage
Blue ammonia captures concentrated process CO2
limitations: Green plants must manage variable renewable power against a steady synthesis loop
Large hydrogen buffer or flexible loop needed
Ammonia toxicity and NOx/N2O in combustion uses
